feedback: Written before this candidate races, so it states no outcome. The candidate is the iteration 8 controller (base_speed 1.1, kp 2.5, ki 0.02, kd 0.8, weights [-1.5 to 1.5], last_direction) with the seven sensors moved from x = +/-0.075 to +/-0.08 m, the allowed limit. It is a single-variable change from the best raced design (iteration 8, score 430.6), so any shift in the per-track numbers can be attributed to span. Iteration 8 showed that widening the array from five to seven sensors lifted s-bend progress from 0.22 to 0.59 and gave one s-bend finish, which supports coverage at large lateral error as a real lever. Iteration 9 showed that raising kp to 3.0 on the same array cut s-bend progress to 0.53 with no finishes, so gain is not the lever and kp stays at 2.5. Slalom is unchanged at progress 0.18, about 1 line-loss event per run, and max_error about 0.063 m, so the outer edge is the thing to test. The 0.027 m spacing leaves a 0.015 m gap between 12 mm footprints, which is smaller than the 25 mm tape, so the tape should always be seen by at least one sensor. The main risk is oval jitter: the outer sensors may read the tape less often at small error. Oval was 20 of 20 at 1.87 s with steering_oscillation 0.17 in iteration 8, so the oval is the main thing to check. Next race, read per track: if the oval stays at 20 of 20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.25 and slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0.5 or below, keep this span and then consider a single controller change. If the oval finish rate drops or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, reduce the outer weights to about 1.2 before changing the array. If slalom still shows line_loss_events near 1 with max_error at or above 0.06 m, the limit is likely turn authority or line loss mode, not coverage. Because this is the last exploration step before the final iteration, keep the best design per track in mind when choosing what to carry forward. Decision: approve, because the candidate is valid, is a clean test of the one hypothesis with the most evidence behind it, and an unscored iteration earns nothing.
requested_changes: If the oval stays at 20 of 20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.25 and slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0.5 or below: keep the 0.08 m span and test one controller change next, such as base_speed 1.2 to recover s-bend progress, since iteration 3 showed speed loss hurts bend progress.

If the oval finish rate drops below 1.0 or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3: keep the 0.08 m span but reduce the outer sensor_weights to about 1.2 (for example [-1.2, -0.8, -0.4, 0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2]) so the effective gain stays near iteration 8.

If slalom still shows line_loss_events near 1 with max_error at or above 0.06 m after the span change: change line_loss from last_direction to search_right, which iteration 9 did not test, before changing kp again, because iteration 9 showed kp 3.0 did not help the bends.
